"# Changelog ## [1.3.0] - 2026-10-15 ### Breaking Changes - Terminology follows the concepts: a reference (what `get` returns) is `Ref` (was `Handle`), its status `RefStatus` (was `HandleStatus`); what a factory returns is `ImplementationOf` (was `BehaviorOf`); a resource's options are a `ResourceDeclaration` (was `ResourceSpec`); epochs are code versions: `Ctx.codeVersion`, `RootOptions.codeVersion`, `Host.codeVersion`/`previousCodeVersion`, and the `codeVersion` fields of frames and reload reports (all were `epoch`). Docs and messages say object (was record) and reference (was handle and hold); the `hold` and `release` frame types keep their names - A remote object's variant is named `variant` (was `kind`): factories return `{ variant: "editor", … }`, references expose `ref.variant` and `shape.variant`, and the `shape` frame carries `variant`. `variant` is reserved as a member name; `kind` no longer is - Links have a protocol version (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`, now 2), announced in `hello`. Peers of different versions do not talk: the side that notices closes the link with reason `protocol-version `, and both sides report it through `LinkOptions.onProtocolMismatch`. Peers without a version (older Chord) are refused - `serve(…, { lifetime })` replaces `eager`: `"referenced"` (the default) creates an object at the first `get` of its address and disposes it after the last reference is released (plus `linger`); `"host"` creates the type's one object when its facet loads and keeps it until the host closes or a reload removes its facet. `lifetime: "host"` is refused at `serve` for remote types, for inputs that do not accept `{}` and together with `linger`; every `get` of such a type reaches its one object, created for the host principal, and another input is `invalid/input`. `eager: { input }` and the extra objects host-principal `get`s with other inputs created are gone. Only `"host"` objects may register (reason `invalid/not_host_lifetime`, was `not_eager`). `LoadOptions.awaitHostObjects` replaces `awaitEager` - Declarations are calls by name: `self.state(name, schema, initial, { version?, migrate? })` returns the cell, `self.resource(name, { version, deps?, exclusive?, open, close? })` the resource (`rev` is now `version`), `self.on(name, source, [select,] handler)` declares a listener; `self.derive(sources, fn)` and `self.task(fn)` take no name. `cell()`, `derivation()`, `resource()`, `listener()`, `self.resources`, `self.listen`, `self.tasks` and the declaration maps are gone, and so are the types `CellDecl`, `ResourceDecl`, `DerivationDecl`, `ListenerDecl`. A repeated name of one kind in a run is `invalid/duplicate` - State versions belong to cells: `ServeOptions.state` is gone; a cell's `version` (default 1) and `migrate(old, from)` replace it. A raised version migrates only that cell; a lowered one refuses the reload - A derivation is new at every reload (computed at the commit) instead of kept with its function replaced. A listener whose state source a reload replaced subscribes again and gets the current value again: listeners on state must reconcile. Listeners on state subscribe when they activate, so they get the value current then - `method(args?, result?)`: without arguments a method is called `ref.name(ctx?)` and implemented `(ctx) => …`; without a result it is void (callers get `undefined`). Descriptions record both by leaving `args`/`result` out (fingerprints of such methods change), `call` frames omit `args` and `result` frames `value` for them. Coverage requires both sides to agree on arguments; a void consumer accepts a result - Remote contracts declare where their objects live, and callers no longer name a host: `remote(name, { …, host: hostNamed("server") })` or `host: hostFamily("session:", "session")` (the host `session:` + the input's required string field `session`, checked by TypeScript). `host` is required on remote contracts; `GetOptions.at` is removed. A `get` normalizes the input, resolves the host, and acquires locally or over the link to it. `serve` refuses a type whose placement does not include the host (also at a reload), a host refuses a hold whose input its own contract places elsewhere (`invalid/placement`), and a relay refuses a hold whose target disagrees with its contract token. The placement is part of the description and fingerprint; coverage requires equal placements, and `accepts` adapters do not bridge placements. Remote references are addressed by type, normalized input and principal, without a host name. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 3 (remote tokens carry `host`; a hold's input is normalized). New exports: `hostNamed`, `hostFamily`, `Placement`, `PlacementFor`, `HostNamed`, `HostFamily` - `FacetApi` has a `signal` (below): code that builds a `FacetApi` by hand, for example to wrap `serve`, must pass it on - Principals are typed and supplied by the app: `createHost

`, `Host

`, `defineFacet

`, `FacetApi

`, `Serve

`, `Factory`, `Self

`, `Ctx

`, `GetOptions

`, `RootOptions

`, `Route

`, `AcceptOptions

` and `PrincipalMatch

` take the app's principal type (default `unknown`), so factories, methods, listeners and tasks narrow on it without casts. Chord invents no principals any more: `createHost({ self })` (required) is the principal of the host's own code, replacing the built-in `hostPrincipal` (`{ host: true }`, removed); `connect(link, { principal })` (required) is what the parent's own requests act as, replacing `{ host: }`; `Route.principal` is required, replacing the default `{ host: }`. `HostOptions.upstream` is `{ link, principal, ...LinkOptions }` (was a link, with `upstreamOptions`). The host's own principal is recognized by `principalKey`, not object identity. The `Principal` type is gone; `ConnectOptions` and `PrincipalPattern` are new - `serve(type, factory, { lifetime: "host" })` compiles only for a local type whose input has no required fields, and without `linger`; `serve` still refuses the rest at runtime. `ServeOptions` is a union of `ReferencedServeOptions` and `HostServeOptions`, and `serve` takes `ServeOptionsFor` - An awaited reference has its state, local or remote. `ctx.get` and `host.get` are async: they resolve once the reference is live and every state member of its variant has its first snapshot, and reject with the activation error, `aborted` (the ctx aborted or its call settled; `host.get`'s `signal`) or `unavailable/ready_timeout` after `HostOptions.readyTimeout` (default 60000 ms), releasing only that reference. `host.hold` is the synchronous form (possibly `loading`) for UI runtimes; `ref.ready` stays. `self.get` stays synchronous: an object goes live only once its references are ready and hydrated, and the state it exposes or derives from (also forwarded from a remote reference held another way) has its values; activation and reload prepare wait at most `readyTimeout` (a reference cycle across hosts fails with a hint instead of hanging) - State members are typed `T` (was `T | undefined`) and `StateSource` is `Readable`. Reading state before the first hydration throws `not_ready`, outside the current variant `not_in_variant`, after the reference ended its end error. A remote reference is a union discriminated by `variant`: another variant's members are reachable only after narrowing. `MembersOf` is gone. A listener added before a member is readable gets its snapshot then (no `undefined` snapshot first) - A remote reference stays subscribed to its variant's state while held, with or without listeners (it no longer forgets its value when the last listener leaves). `GetOptions.state: false` makes a method-only reference: no state unless another reference to the object wants it, ready once live - `Shape.codeVersion` and the `shape` frame's `codeVersion` are gone - `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 4: a `hold` implies the state of its variant (`state: false` opts out until `sub`; `unsub` stops it); the provider answers with units, a `shape` listing the members the consumer lacks (`state`) followed by their snapshots; `state` frames are addressed by hold and member (`hold`, `m`) with `as: "snap" | "reset" | "ops" | "error"` and `value` (absent: `undefined`); `sub`/`unsub` take a hold; `resync` asks for a member again; `again` marks a re-hold after a link loss; `origin` (replacing `client`) names the client connection a hold comes from ### Added - `@earendil-works/chord/output`: `OutputBuffer`, which keeps a head or tail window of a stream at a cost proportional to each chunk, `Progress`, which paces commits of a changing value by their size, plus `boundOutput`, `sanitizeOutput`, `characterEnd`, `utf8ByteLength`, and the `OutputLimits`, `BoundedOutput`, `OutputSlice`, and `OutputSkip` types. Moved from `@earendil-works/pi-durable`, which now uses them from here. - Remote references to one object share one binding per host and key (type, normalized input identity, principal key, contract fingerprint): one hold, one stream per state member, calls over the same hold; every reference keeps its own status, observers and `release`. `HostOptions.linger` (`{ types: { [typeName]: ms }, cap }`, cap default 4) keeps a binding held and hydrated after its last reference is released, so a reference taken again meanwhile costs nothing on the link - Holds from clients carry an opaque `origin`: the id the accepting host gave the client connection, forwarded by relays and honored only from the parent link, so a host can tell client connections apart; a disconnect releases that client's holds at once - Flow control by units: the first unit of a new reference passes the window, so a `get` never waits behind other references' state; units for reloads and re-holds wait, built lazily from the current values; waiting ops are capped per link (`LinkOptions.pendingCap`, default four windows), beyond which the oldest streams become resets (a relay asks downstream with `resync`) - `StateOptions`, `EventOf`, `ValueOf` and `Lifetime` types - `self.state(name, schema, { init }, options?)`: a cell whose first value comes from its source. `init(ctx)` (may be async) runs once the object's resources are open and its references live, before the object goes live, so no method, listener, task or subscriber sees another value; a throw or an invalid value fails the activation. A reload keeps the cell without running `init`; a cell a reload adds runs it while the reload prepares (a failure refuses the reload). Until then the cell's `value` throws `not_ready`. `StateInit` type - Links are flow controlled end to end: peers acknowledge what they processed (`ack` frames, announced with `acks` in `hello`), and while a window of frames is unacknowledged (`window` in `LinkOptions`, default 256 KiB), state frames wait at the sender, coalesced per subscription, instead of queuing in front of call results. A stalled peer costs a bounded slot per subscription; a slot that outgrows it becomes a reset. Calls, results and control frames are never held back, so under load a result can arrive before state changes made before it - `maxCalls` in `AcceptOptions` limits the calls a peer may have in progress on a link; further ones are answered at once with `unavailable` (reason `too_many_calls`) and the link stays open - `FacetApi.signal` aborts once that run of the facet is no longer installed: a committed reload replaced or removed it, the reload that loaded it aborted, or the host closed. While a reload prepares, the installed and the candidate run are both live - `HostOptions.taskStopDeadline` (default 5000 ms) bounds how long a reload waits for aborted tasks before it starts their replacements - Links deflate call arguments, results and state snapshots whose JSON exceeds `PACK_THRESHOLD` (64K characters): over IPC as a base64 field, over WebSockets as a binary message. Relaying hosts forward the deflated bytes unread; the host that uses the payload inflates it. `webSocketLink(socket, { compress, acceptPacked })` (`WebSocketLinkOptions`) controls sending and accepting packed frames (servers should refuse them from untrusted clients), and `inflateMessage` turns a packed WebSocket message back into a text frame ### Changed - `Link.send` returns the encoded frame's size as sent (deflated payloads count as sent) when the transport knows it (memory and WebSocket links); flow control counts these sizes, so links that return nothing (IPC, custom links) are not windowed - A reload starts an object's new tasks only after its aborted ones finished (at most `taskStopDeadline`, then anyway, reported); before, the old and the new run of a task worked side by side - When a reload forces the retirement of the previous code version, it first aborts the roots still running on it (their `ctx.signal`, reason `superseded`) and gives them up to 1 s to stop before it closes what only that code used; a call with such a ctx is `superseded`. Before, resources were closed under running roots, which were never told ### Fixed - `nodeLoader` registers every facet's directory before importing any, so a facet that imports a file of a facet listed after it gets the same module copy as that facet; before, the load order could produce duplicates. - A link that is already closed when a host accepts or routes to it is no longer kept as a connection: before, a route that returned a dead link (a child process that exited before its link was wrapped) made every later call to that host name fail with `unavailable` until restart, and leaked the connection's ping timer. - Fixed `processLock()` failing with `listen EINVAL` on macOS and the BSDs when the temporary directory is too deep for a socket path (sun_path holds 104 bytes); the lock socket then lives in a private per-user directory, `/tmp/chord2-` - A child host whose hello arrived while a cluster reload ran was marked in step without taking part, so it stayed on the old code version and every call to it failed `superseded` until it reconnected. It is now synced or reconciled when the reload ends; a child already behind is fenced at once, so its roots' calls up are admitted meanwhile. A reconciliation that is running when a reload starts likewise syncs its child only after that reload, against the committed code version - A child host retired its previous code version as soon as a cluster reload's `prepare` arrived, before its parent did, so the parent's old roots got `superseded` on it. The coordinator now retires before it sends `prepare`, a child waits for its parent's `retire` (at most `retireDeadline`), and a child coming in step (or about to be reconciled) is told which code versions the parent retired before - Disposed objects stayed reachable from the host until an object with the same address was created again (every distinct guest, session or input leaked one object, its references and the code they bind) - References kept every code version's services, and with them the factory code of every reload, reachable for as long as they lived (held references, objects of lifetime `"host"`); old code generations could never be collected - Call, task and root contexts were linked to long-lived signals with `AbortSignal.any`; Node keeps such dependants reachable while they have abort listeners, so a listener on `ctx.signal` kept its closure (and its code generation) alive for the object's lifetime. Contexts now detach when they close - IPC links and the host manager's control channel wrote to a peer process that had exited without a callback, so the `EPIPE` Node reports for a write in the gap between the exit and `disconnect` (an `ack` sent just after a worker shut down) became an unhandled `error` event that crashed the process. The link now ends on a failed write (reason `ipc send failed: EPIPE`), and control messages to a gone peer are dropped - A relayed call ran under the origin's cancel signal only, so a forced retirement of the relaying host could not cancel it before closing the old code's resources; it now follows its root's signal - A resource kept across a reload closed with the `close` of the factory run that first opened it, and kept that run's code reachable; it now adopts the newest declaration at commit - `forkDriver` passed its own `CHORD2_LOCK` to forked children, so a child host that forked its own children made those without a lock of their own fail with `locked` - A call through a remote reference accepted a ctx from another host, or an object not made by Chord, and carried its root over the link; it now rejects it with `invalid/foreign_ctx` like a local reference ([#10959](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10959)) ## [1.2.0] - 2026-10-12 ### Breaking Changes - Replaced the facet and service runtime with a typed host runtime: contracts (`local`, `remote`, `method`, `opaque`) are runtime values described with TypeBox schemas, objects are served by hosts (`createHost`, `defineFacet`, `defineRegistry`) and reached through handles, and hosts exchange JSON frames over memory, Node IPC, or WebSocket links (`memoryLinkPair`, `ipcLink`, `webSocketLink`, `acceptWebSockets`), with hot reload of plugins. See `docs/tutorial.md` and `docs/guide.md` - Removed `defineService`, `createFacetHost`, `createRemoteServiceBinding`, `createStaticFacetLoader`, `combineFacetLoaders`, the remote-service endpoint, provider, error, and wire helpers, and their types. The old `defineFacet`, `Facet`, and `FacetLoader` are replaced by the new runtime's names of the same spelling - Removed the `./bundler` export and the facet bundle loaders of `./node`; `./node` now exports the child host manager (`createHostManager`, `forkDriver`, `childControl`, `processLock`) and the facet module loader `nodeLoader` - Removed `@earendil-works/pi-client`, `@earendil-works/pi-protocol`, and `@earendil-works/pi-server`, which served only the old runtime; they are no longer released ### Changed - `replicatedState`, `copyJson`, `isJsonValue`, `Context`, `JsonValue`, `JsonRepresentation`, `Draft`, and the replicated state types keep their names on the root export; `./context` and `./delta` are unchanged, and `./context` also exports the `Context` and `ContextKey` types - Depends on `typebox` instead of `esbuild` ### Fixed - Fixed appending to an array costing a walk over the whole array: the delta tracker now plans inserts and removals that keep the remaining elements in order from the changed ranges alone, and `applyImmutable` builds an appended array in one copy instead of two. 32,000 one-item appends, one commit each, take 1.4 s instead of 11.3 s "

"# Chord specification This document specifies the runtime in `src`. Where it and the code disagree, the disagreement is a bug. [Known limitations and decisions](#12-known-limitations-and-decisions) lists what the runtime does not do yet and the choices the sections below leave open. Hard constraints: - Chord's runtime depends only on its own `delta` module (tracker, applyImmutable, encoder/decoder, diff) and Node/browser built-ins plus `typebox` for schemas. No other Pi packages. - Built-in plugins are trusted, loaded from source in-process. The plugin loader uses dynamic `import()` with a cache-busting query (owner-approved exception, `TODO(loader)`: replace with an isolating, evicting loader; old module copies leak; TUI plugins need isolation). - Hot reload is required. Host restart only for Chord/runtime code changes or host-level crash recovery. ## 1. Concepts | Term | Meaning | | --- | --- | | facet | A plugin's code for one host (surface): it serves object types (`defineFacet`). | | object type | Name + contract. `remote` (addressable from other hosts; schemas for input, variant state members, method args/results) or `local` (host-only; members may be anything, including functions and native objects, but must be listed in the contract: `method`, `opaque` or a state schema). | | factory | `(input, principal, self) => implementation`. Synchronous. Registered with `host.serve(type, factory, options)` from a plugin facet. | | object | One instance of an object type. Stable identity per `(type, canonicalInput, principalKey)`. Owns cells, resources, references, listeners, tasks, registrations. Survives reloads. | | implementation | The object's code: what a factory run returns (methods + state members; `variant` for remote types). Immutable, per code version. | | reference | What `get` returns: a late-bound claim on an object, never the object or its implementation. An object lives while referenced. | | principal | App-defined. Stamped by links. In-host code acts as the `host` principal. | | root | One short Chord call tree, admitted at trusted ingress (link request without root, UI event, timer, `host.root`). Carries `{ rootId, codeVersion }`. | | code version | One committed set of implementations/registrations per host (server-issued id). | | code holder | Long-lived execution that is NOT a root: Durable phases/tool runs, browsers, `self.task` loops. Every Chord call they make starts a fresh short root. | ## 2. Contracts Contracts are runtime values for every type (shipped bundles have no TypeScript; third-party plugins are built separately). TS types are inferred from them. ```ts export const Chat = remote("pi.chat", { version: 1, // contract version: a plain number, bumped only on breaking changes input: Type.Object({ session: Type.String(), conversation: Type.Number() }), host: hostFamily("session:", "session"), // where its objects live: `session:` + input.session variants: { viewer: { state: { view: ViewSchema } }, participant: { state: { view: ViewSchema }, methods: { send: method(SendSchema, Type.Object({ submissionId: Type.Number() })) }, }, }, }); export const Index = local("pi.index", { version: 1, input: Type.Object({ session: Type.String() }), members: { search: method(Type.Object({ query: Type.String() }), Type.Array(Hit)), onChange: method(Type.Function([Change], Type.Void()), Unsubscribe), // non-JSON allowed for locals harness: opaque("pi.durable-harness@1"), // native object, by name+version }, }); ``` - Input identity: normalize (apply defaults, strip unknown), validate, then canonical JSON with fields equal to their schema default omitted. Changing defaults or normalization requires a new type name. - Remote calls validate args/results and state values at the provider boundary. Local calls are not validated per call. - Local contracts list every member (`members: { search: method(...), harness: opaque(...), status: Schema }`). A reference that is still `loading` must know whether `h.x` is a method (a caller that waits until live), a state member (a readable) or an opaque value, before any implementation exists. Members missing from the contract are found only once the reference is live. - Every bundle embeds the contract tokens it was built against (its own copy). Fingerprint = hash of the canonical description. - Placement (remote types, required): `host: hostNamed(name)` (one host) or `hostFamily(prefix, key)` (the host `prefix` + the input's required string field `key`). Data only, in the description (and so the fingerprint and the `hold` token); there is no `at` option. A `get` normalizes the input with the caller's contract, resolves the host and acquires locally if that is this host, else remotely. `serve` (and a reload that loads a facet) refuses a type whose placement excludes the host's name. A host refuses a hold whose input its own contract places elsewhere (`invalid/placement`), and a relay refuses a hold whose target disagrees with its token's placement and input. Coverage requires equal placements, and an `accepts` adapter never bridges two placements: a moved type is a breaking change. A remote reference's address is the type, the normalized input and the principal: no host name. ### Compatibility rule A consumer built against version M binds to a provider at version N iff N = M and the provider's description covers the consumer's; otherwise only through `accepts[M]` adapters declared by the provider (`serve(type, factory, { accepts: { 1: (current) => v1View } })`); else `contract_mismatch`. Covers: every consumer member exists with the same kind; methods: both take arguments or neither does, the provider accepts every argument the consumer can send (new fields optional, nothing newly required or retyped), and the provider's result fits the consumer's expected result (extra fields fine; a void consumer accepts any); state: provider value fits consumer schema (extra fields fine); opaque: same name@version. Additive changes need no bump. Breaking changes (remove/rename/retype, newly required, or a change of meaning with the same shape) bump the number. Same version + non-covering description = forgotten bump, refused. Meaning changes without a bump are undetectable (author's responsibility, as with Durable document versions). Checked at: `get` binding, reload prepare (new provider token vs every surviving consumer holding the type and every loaded plugin importing it), remote references (consumer token in the `hold` frame). Without `migrate`, a raised version keeps the value, which must fit the new schema. **Listeners on state reconcile.** A listener whose source is state (a cell, a derivation, a reference's state member) is subscribed when it starts and gets the current value, then every new value. A reload that replaces its source (every derivation is new; a reference to another address is another source) subscribes it again, so it gets the current value again: its handler must reconcile (be idempotent), not count events. An event source (a resource's events, any other `subscribe`) delivers no current value; a kept subscription to it is not touched by a reload. **Methods.** `method(args?, result?)`: without `args` the method takes none (callers `ref.name(ctx?)`, implementation `(ctx) => …`; `method(undefined, result)` for one that returns something); without `result` it is void (callers get `undefined`, whatever the implementation returned). The description records both (absent fields), and the `call` frame carries no `args` and the `result` frame no `value` for them. Removed vs guide: `self.own`, `holdWhile`, async factories, inferred dependencies. ### Synchronous factory, asynchronous activation `self.get` and `self.resource` only declare and return placeholders. Activation of an object: 1. run the factory synchronously (declarations); 2. await declared resources' `open()` (e.g. connect a DB); 3. await declared references becoming live (dependencies activate first, coalesced); 4. run the `init` of every cell declared with one, in parallel, each in a root of its own acting as the host principal; validate and install the values; 5. attach derivations, start listeners and tasks; 6. object is live: references `live`, `ready` resolves. Inside the factory, placeholders must not be used (`resource.value` and an `init` cell's `value` throw `not_ready`; reference calls throw). An `init` that throws, or returns a value its schema refuses, fails the activation like a failed `open`. An `init` must not wait for its own object or one that holds it (it is not live yet), and must not read another `init` cell of its object (they run in parallel). `init` gives a first value from a source the object reads anyway; it does not persist anything, and a cell is not saved anywhere by having one. Methods/listeners/tasks run only on live objects, so their dependencies are live. An object goes live only once its references are ready (live and, for remote ones, hydrated) and the state sources it exposes or derives from have their values, also where they forward a remote reference held some other way; waiting for references is bounded by the host's `readyTimeout` (default 60 s, `unavailable/ready_timeout`, also for a reference cycle across hosts). External consumers holding a `loading` reference (`host.hold`): calls wait until live (ctx cancellation, deadline); state members throw `not_ready` until the first hydration. Activation failures propagate to dependents and all waiting gets; the next get retries. ### Lifetime `serve(type, factory, { lifetime })`: | `lifetime` | Created | Ends | `linger` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `"referenced"` (default) | at the first `get` of its address | after the last reference is released, plus `linger` | allowed (default 0) | | `"host"` | when its facet loads (or at `serve`); loading waits until it is live | when the host closes, or a reload removes its facet | refused | - `"host"` is refused at `serve` for remote types, for an input that does not accept `{}`, and together with `linger`; the types (`ServeOptionsFor`) refuse the same at compile time, where such an input is one with a required field. The type has exactly one object: the empty input (defaults applied), created for the host principal. Every `get` reaches it, whatever its principal (the factory sees the host principal); a `get` with another input is `invalid/input`. Other references do not change its lifetime: the host keeps its own until it closes. - Only `"host"` objects may register (`invalid/not_host_lifetime` otherwise). - A `"host"` object whose activation fails is started again by the next reload that changes its type. A reload that makes a type `"host"` creates its object; one that makes it `"referenced"` releases the host's reference, so the object lives on only while others reference it. ### Host objects readiness - `host.install(facet, { awaitHostObjects? })` installs declarations synchronously and returns a promise for this facet's host object activations. `host.load(facets, { awaitHostObjects? })` installs the entire batch before awaiting its host object activations. `awaitHostObjects` defaults to true. Unreferenced objects are not activated. - Factory, resource-open, dependency and activation-finalization failures reject the returned promise with the activation error (ChordError codes preserved; ordinary errors wrapped as `unavailable`). Host object failures also reach `onError`. Installation is not a rollback transaction; setup/registration errors from `install` throw synchronously. Abandoned startup should close the host. - `{ awaitHostObjects: false }` starts the same host objects but resolves after installation, without waiting for their activation. `host.ready()` awaits a snapshot of the host's references to its host objects at call time (including direct `serve` and deferred loads), rejects their activation failures, and does not acquire additional references. It is not an ongoing health check and does not await task completion or remote state hydration. - Local bootstrap readiness and upstream admission are separate. A worker connects its upstream link, loads with `{ awaitHostObjects: false }`, awaits its local bootstrap reference (e.g. Harness, with no upstream dependency), then announces control readiness so its parent can accept the link. Only after admission does it await `host.ready()`. Otherwise a host object reporting to the server's SessionStatus deadlocks with the parent waiting for control readiness. Deferred loads skip the whole barrier, not selected dependencies; callers explicitly choose local bootstrap references, keep bootstrap busy until full readiness, and propagate later startup errors. ## 4. They reject with the activation error, `aborted` (ctx aborted or settled, `signal`), or `unavailable/ready_timeout`, releasing only that reference. `host.hold` is the synchronous form for UI runtimes. A held remote reference stays subscribed to its variant's state until released; after a link loss its last values stay readable while it re-holds. State members are typed `T`; reading before the first hydration throws `not_ready`, outside the variant `not_in_variant`, after the end the end's error. A remote reference type is a union discriminated by `variant`. Shape changes (reload, variant) are pushed; members missing from the current variant reject `not_in_variant`; released references reject `released`; forced disposal makes references `gone`. - Shared bindings: remote references on a host with the same key (type, normalized input identity, principal key, consumer contract fingerprint) are views onto one binding: one hold, one stream per state member, calls over that hold. Views have their own owner (object, call, external), status, observers and `release`; the binding ends (gone) or re-holds for all of them. Without views a binding closes, or lingers for `linger.types[typeName]` ms (`createHost({ linger: { types, cap } })`, at most `cap`, default 4, least recently released first) while staying held and hydrated. - Methods are `(args, ctx) => Promise`. Lifetime - Reference owners: object (declared `get`), call (`ctx.get`, released at settle), connection (remote references; relay maps per origin connection), host (`lifetime: "host"`), UI. - Activation coalesced per address; if all requesters leave before it completes, the result is disposed. Factory throw: unwind declarations, reject gets, next get retries. - Disposal after the last reference is released + `linger`: tasks aborted, listeners removed, resources closed (reverse order; all run; errors aggregated), the object's references released (cascade). - Bulk forced disposal (`host.close`, `invalidatePrincipal`) goes in waves, referrers before what they reference, so a resource's `close` can still use its object's references; `host.close` closes links after the objects. - Forced disposal: references `gone` immediately, new calls rejected, in-flight call contexts aborted, then cooperative cleanup. - Reference graph acyclic in-host (checked at get); across hosts by convention. - Links have ping/timeout; a dead link releases everything held through it. ## 6. Roots and code versions - `Ctx = { signal, rootId, codeVersion, get(...): Promise, principal? }`. Explicit; no AsyncLocalStorage dependency (may be used in dev to warn). - A link creates a root for a request that carries none; nested remote calls carry `{rootId, codeVersion}`. - Dispatch: a call with code version E runs the object's implementation for E. A host retains at most `current` and `previous` code versions (two-version rule). A call for a code version the host doesn't have (older than previous, or host started later) is rejected `superseded` (retryable by starting a new root). Never substitute another code version. - Browsers never carry code versions into the server: browser calls start roots at the server. Browsers learn of changes via shape/reset pushes and a server `Manifest` object; incompatible contract fingerprint -> `upgrade_required`. ## 7. Reload Explicit trigger (`reload_plugins` tool, button, API). Serialized; no nesting. 1. Build/type-check gate (application tooling, outside Chord): dependency-closed set; refuse breaking remote contract changes without a contract version bump. 2. Load: on every affected host, import new facet modules (cache-busted). 3. Prepare: for each live object of each affected type, run the new factory in recording mode: existing cells readable, writes throw; listeners/tasks/registrations recorded, not started; references recorded; non-exclusive resources whose name is new or whose `version`/`deps` changed are opened as candidate-owned (closed on abort). Validate keys, variants, registry collisions. New objects activated during prepare use the current code version (old code). Any failure: abort, discard candidates. Vote. 4. Gate (only objects with a cell whose version was raised or which replace an exclusive resource, plus objects depending on those resources): - Admission cut: from now, an old-code-version root that has not touched the object gets `upgrade_conflict` (retryable), not queued. Roots that already hold an activation lease on it are grandfathered; their re-entry is admitted. - Wait for grandfathered activations to finish, deadline (default 5 s). Missed deadline: abort the reload, reopen, nothing changed (report blocking roots). - Exclusive resources: close old, open new; on failure reopen old and abort. - Run `migrate` into private copies; validate. 5. Commit (server commits itself, then sends commit to children; the decision is not persisted, see section 12; FIFO links guarantee no host receives a new-code-version root before committing): each host in one synchronous step installs migrated cell values and cell versions, installs implementations as code version E', swaps registry tables, restarts tasks with new code, rebinds listeners, pushes shape/reset to subscribers, opens gates. E' current, E previous. The coordinator's result carries `children`: each participating child's prepared report (its vote). 6. Retire: when no roots of `previous` remain (and, on a child, the parent retired it), drop its implementations and release declarations only it declared. The next reload first waits for that, at most `retireDeadline`; then it aborts the roots still running on `previous` (their ctx signals), gives them up to 1 s to stop, and retires anyway. A coordinator retires before it sends `prepare`, so its `retire` frames reach the children first. Compatible changes (no state bump, no exclusive resource change) skip the gate: no waiting. State compatibility rule: reload prepare compares each cell's old and new schema and version. Unchanged: compatible (no gate). Version raised: gate + `migrate` (or the kept value), validated against the new schema. Schema changed without a raised version: reload refused. A lowered version: refused. A change of meaning with an identical schema needs a bump too (undetectable; author's responsibility). Initial values and migrate outputs are validated; per-write validation in dev mode. ## 8. Registries ```ts export const Routes = defineRegistry("http.routes", { conflict: "error" }); self.register(Routes, { "GET /download": handler }); // in a `lifetime: "host"` object; keys are the registry's keys host.registry(Routes).get("GET /download", ctx); // table of ctx.codeVersion (or current without ctx) host.registry(Routes).subscribe((table, codeVersion) => ...); // bridges for imperative consumers (Durable) ``` Per-code-version immutable tables; order = first registration order, kept on replace. An application can implement Durable's `RegistryReader` from the table (snapshot per code version) so phases pin a complete snapshot; Chord does not ship that bridge. ## 9. Hosts and links - `createHost({ name, self, principalKey, upstream?: { link, principal } })`; `host.accept(link, { principal })` for children; `host.connect(link, { principal })` for the parent; `host.route(prefix, { authorize(principal, hostName), resolve(hostName) => Promise, principal(hostName) })`. - Links: `memoryLinkPair()` (tests), Node IPC (child_process), WebSocket (server `ws`, browser `WebSocket`). - Principal stamping: the accepting side stamps the principal of what connects (from its authenticator); forwarded principals accepted only from the parent link; the parent's own requests (no forwarded principal) act as the principal given to `connect`; payload principal fields ignored. - A child that connects behind its parent's code version is fenced (nothing routed to it) and reconciled by a reload of its modules to the parent's code version. Calls its roots of the old code version make upstream are admitted in the parent's current code version (the parent never ran that code version), not rejected `superseded`. - Relay: server forwards a hold to the child link of its target host (`at`, resolved by the consumer from the contract's placement and the normalized input, and checked against both), mapping references per origin connection; authorizes before resolving/spawning and re-checks after. - Wire frames (JSON): `hello`/`bye`, `hold`/`release` (a reference over a link: `hold` returns `shape` or `gone`; there is no separate `get`), `shape`, `call`/`result`/`cancel`, `sub`/`unsub`/`resync` and `state`, `gone`, `root_end`, `retire`, `invalidate`, `ping`/`pong`, `ack`, reload control (`prepare`/`vote`/`commit`/`abort`). - State: a `hold` implies the state of its variant (`state: false`: none until `sub`; `unsub` stops it). The provider answers with units: a `shape` whose `state` lists the members the consumer lacks, followed by one `state` frame `as: "snap"` per listed member; the consumer applies the shape once those snapshots are here. Later `state` frames of a member (addressed by hold id and member `m`) are `ops` (per-stream delta encoder), `reset`, or `error`; a `snap`/`reset` without `value` carries `undefined`. A failed snapshot before the first hydration ends the reference with its error. A reload or variant change sends a unit with the members that are new; members that left stop. `again` marks a re-hold after a link loss (the consumer has values). `origin` names the client connection a hold comes from (stamped by the host that accepted the client, forwarded by relays, honored only from the parent link). - Protocol version: `hello` carries `protocol` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`, now 4; absent means 1). A side that sees another version processes nothing more, calls `LinkOptions.onProtocolMismatch({ local, peer })` and closes the link with reason `protocol-version `; the other side's connection reads that reason and reports the mismatch too. Peers do not negotiate: the outdated side must load the current code (a browser reloads its page). Frame fields follow the version: the `shape` frame names the variant `variant`, code versions travel as `codeVersion` (2); remote contract tokens carry their placement (`host`), and a `hold` carries the input normalized by the consumer (3); a hold implies its state, units, `origin`, and `shape` without a code version (4). - Flow control: both ends announce `acks` in their hello and acknowledge what they processed (`ack`, a cumulative count of every frame but `ack`). While the frames not yet acknowledged exceed the window (`window`, default 256 KiB of JSON text), state waits at the sender in slots flushed in creation order: one per member stream (ops are appended, a snapshot or reset replaces it, a release or `unsub` drops it) and one per hold for a unit (lazy: built from the current values when sent; a newer unit merges into it). Waiting ops are capped per link (`pendingCap`, default four windows): beyond, the oldest streams become a reset of their current value built at flush (a relay sends `resync` downstream and drops that member's ops until the reset arrives). The first unit of a hold that is not `again` and every frame but state are sent at once. Links that report no frame sizes (IPC) are never windowed; a peer without `acks` is neither windowed nor acknowledged. An acceptor can limit the calls a peer has in progress (`maxCalls`); calls beyond it are answered at once with `unavailable/too_many_calls`. Nothing outside the connection may add frames to a link: acknowledgements count them. ## 10. Test coverage The tests cover at least: lifetime/references/linger/forced disposal/gone; activation coalescing and abandonment; principals and variants; remote calls over memory links incl. relay and principal forgery attempts; state snap/ops/reset over a link with reconnect; registries per code version; reload: compatible (no wait, pinned roots), prepare isolation (writes throw, failing factory leaves everything unchanged), state bump with migrate and gate, `upgrade_conflict` for late old roots, deadline abort, exclusive resource replacement, cross-host commit ordering, two-version retirement and `superseded`. ## 12. Known limitations and decisions ### Still open - **Retirement across hosts.** A child retires a code version only after its parent retired it (`retire` frame) and its own roots of that code version ended; the server decides from its own roots. A child that comes in step (hello or reconciliation) is told which code versions the parent retired before. A root started on a worker that calls up to a server which has already retired the code version both had still gets `superseded` (retryable). - **The commit decision is not persisted** (section 7, step 5). A server crash between its own commit and a child's commit leaves that child on the old code version until it reconnects and is reconciled. - **One level of reload participants.** Only the coordinator's direct child hosts take part; a child does not forward `prepare` to its own children. - **Reconciliation needs the child's module list.** It is remembered from cluster reloads (`host.remoteModules`), so a server restart forgets it, and a child behind a restarted server then reloads no modules: it gets the code version id with its own code. The reconciliation vote deadline is fixed at 30 s; a failed reconciliation closes the link, so the host manager restarts the worker. - **Links do not resume.** The provider releases everything held through a closed link at once, so re-held objects are new ones. Keeping references for a reconnect window would need session ids on links. Calls in flight when a link drops reject `unavailable`; whether they ran is unknown. - **Refused clients cannot tell.** The WebSocket adapter closes unauthenticated sockets; the client sees a dropped upstream and its calls wait for a reconnect until their ctx is aborted. - **The publication queue is process-wide and synchronous.** A slow observer delays every later notification in the process, including those of other hosts in the same process. - **No automatic restart.** A terminal host failure is picked up by the host manager's `keepAlive` or `fatal` path, not inside Chord. - **The Node loader leaks.** Every reload imports fresh module copies that are never evicted, and it does not isolate plugins (`TODO(loader)`). - **Stale socket locks.** On Unix systems other than Linux, two processes that probe the same stale socket file at the same moment could both take the lock. Managers serialize starts per lock name. - **Listener `select` identity.** A listener's subscription is kept across factory runs when its origin and `select` are unchanged; `select` counts as unchanged when identical or with the same source text, so a `select` whose implementation depends on captured values that change between runs is not detected. - **Shutdown and dead links.** `host.close()` disposes objects in waves (referrers before what they reference) and closes links last. A `close` that awaits a remote call over a link that is already down waits for a reconnect; bound such calls. ### Decisions - **Errors.** The guide's codes; a `reason` field carries the detail, for example `invalid/args`, `invalid/cycle`, `invalid/duplicate`, `invalid/read_only`, `invalid/not_host_lifetime`, `invalid/registry_conflict`, or `unavailable/unknown_type`. A `ChordError` thrown by a factory or a dependency keeps its code through every dependent; other errors become `unavailable`, with the original as `cause`. - **Reload errors.** There is no `reload_aborted` code. A failed reload throws the cause's code and reason with the message `reload aborted: …` (the cause is attached). Reasons of its own are `aborted/gate_deadline` (with the blocking roots in `details`), `aborted/deadline`, `aborted/vote_deadline` and `unavailable/reload_running`. Across hosts, the message names the host that failed. A child cannot reload on its own (`unavailable/not_coordinator`). - **New objects during prepare.** A reload pre-allocates the next code version ("pending"). Types the same reload adds are served from it; their objects install implementation only for the pending code version and are force-disposed if the reload aborts. - **Gate admission.** From the gate until commit or abort, creating a new object of a changed type fails with `upgrade_conflict` (retryable, reason `gate`); nothing is paused, so nothing can deadlock. Gated objects get `minCodeVersion = E'`: calls and writes carrying an older code version are rejected `upgrade_conflict` permanently, and a gated object drops its previous-code-version implementation at commit. Only objects whose cell versions or exclusive resources change are gated. - **Tasks and listeners during the gate.** Tasks of gated objects are aborted at the admission cut and restart with new code at commit, or with the old code on abort. Listener events for gated objects are queued and replayed through the new listener at commit, or the old one at abort. - **Grandfathered roots** are the roots that called into the object and are still running at the cut. Every host remembers on which links a root's calls went out and sends `root_end` on them when the root ends, so leases outlive calls across hosts. - **Removed types and missed retirement.** Objects of removed types are force-disposed at commit. When a retirement deadline is missed, retirement is forced: those roots are aborted first (their ctx signal, reason `superseded`; a relayed call's root cancels its downstream call), then what only that code version declared is closed, and their next call is `superseded`. - **Joining during a reload.** Participants are the child hosts in step when a reload starts. A child whose hello arrives while it runs is decided when it ends: in step, or reconciled to the committed code version; a child already behind is fenced at once, so the calls its roots make meanwhile are admitted in the parent's code version. A reconciliation that is running when a reload starts syncs its child only after that reload ended, against the code version it committed. A reconciliation announces the parent's retired code versions before its `prepare`. - **Two-version rule.** An object of a changed type created after a commit has only new code; a previous-code-version root calling it gets `superseded`. - **Validation.** Remote calls are validated at reference dispatch, in-host too: a direct binding against the provider's schema, a binding through an adapter against the consumer's. A provider validates each snapshot and reset of a remote state member once per (re)subscription, against the consumer's contract through an `accepts` adapter and the provider's otherwise; ops are validated only in dev mode. At reload, the new provider's description must cover the old provider's when the version is unchanged, in addition to the check against live consumers and facets' `uses`. - **Contracts.** Local contracts list their members, so a loading reference knows whether a member is a method, state or opaque. Canonical identity omits input fields equal to their default; with TypeBox, use `Type.Optional(Type.X({ default }))` to let callers omit them. Provider variants must cover consumer variants; members the consumer's contract does not list are hidden. Schema change detection compares canonical JSON, so reordering `anyOf` branches counts as a change. Fingerprints use a non-cryptographic 64-bit hash: synchronous and browser-safe; contracts are trusted. - **Principals.** A root ctx at ingress acts as its principal (`host.root(fn, { principal })`); contexts inside objects act as `host`. The acceptor decides a link's kind and name (`accept(link, { principal, kind, name })`); only configured host links are addressable, carry roots and may vote, and control frames are accepted only from the parent. Clients never carry roots or code versions. Relaying needs a matching `route`; `authorize(principal, hostName)` runs before `resolve` and again after, and revoking or re-stamping a principal closes its relays at once. `invalidatePrincipal(match)` re-stamps or closes matching links and propagates pattern matches to child hosts. - **Cells and readables.** A value returned from `change` replaces the value and is always validated; `replace` transfers ownership without copying; by default (`{ diff }` overrides) it publishes a diff when the new value reuses a container of the old one at the same key, else `r`. `subscribe(fn)` delivers values, starting with the current one; `events(fn)` delivers `snap`, then `ops`, or `reset`. Reference state members are stable readables that throw `not_ready` while loading and `not_in_variant` outside the variant, and reset when their source moves; a listener added before they are readable gets its snapshot then. Remote state members stay hydrated while the reference is held. - **References and calls.** A reference's identity is its address; a second `self.get` of the same address in one run returns the same reference. A reference call without ctx, or with a task ctx, starts a fresh root in the current code version; a ctx whose call or root already settled is refused (`aborted/expired`), one from another host `invalid/foreign_ctx`. Calling a reference inside a factory throws `not_ready`. - **Resources and disposal.** New and replaced exclusive resources open at the gate, and so do non-exclusive resources of the same object that depend on them. A new object for an address that is still being disposed waits for that disposal. A resource open that completes after its signal aborted closes its value at once. - **Links and the host manager.** Every received frame is validated against its schema; malformed frames, duplicate ids and control frames from the wrong side close the link. Each connection pings every `pingInterval` and closes after `pingTimeout` without a frame. The child holds a kernel lock (an abstract socket on Linux and Android, a named pipe on Windows, a probed socket file elsewhere), acquired by `childControl().lock()` before storage opens. The manager kills the child's process group on every exit path and derives `booting` and `idleFor` from the child's liveness reports. WebSocket support is structural, so Chord does not depend on `ws`. - **Flow control holds back state only.** A relay (Cloudflare to a browser) can hide a slow reader, so transport backpressure cannot be relied on; acknowledgements are end to end. Results must not wait behind state, so links are FIFO except that waiting state frames can be overtaken: a result may arrive before state changes made before it. Frames of one subscription stay in order. Waiting state is coalesced rather than queued and capped per link, so a stalled peer costs bounded memory, and the next frame it gets is current. The first unit of a new reference is not held back, so a `get` never waits behind other streams. - **The state API stays.** Objects keep named cells and unnamed derivations; giving each object exactly one state value was rejected. Do not reopen this without a new, concrete problem. "

"# Chord Delta

Chord Delta produces immutable JSON revisions and exact operation batches for
ordered replicas. Import it from `@earendil-works/chord/delta`.

Immutability is an ownership contract. Nothing is frozen or defensively copied,
so an illegal mutation is not detected. It silently corrupts state.

```ts
import { applyImmutable, applyImmutableBatches, track } from "@earendil-works/chord/delta";

const initial = { output: "", entries: [] as { id: number }[] };
const tracker = track(initial); // `initial` is transferred: never mutate it again

const change = tracker.beginChange();
change.state.output += "done\n"; // the draft is mutable only while the change is open
change.state.entries.push({ id: 1 }); // placed values are cloned; the caller keeps its object
const prepared = change.prepare(); // draft handles are unusable from here on

// tracker.value, prepared.base, prepared.value, and prepared.ops (including paths
// and payloads) are immutable by contract.
tracker.adopt(prepared); // tracker.value === prepared.value

// Shares containers with prepared.base and the op payloads: never mutate it either.
const replica = applyImmutable(prepared.base, prepared.ops);
```

## Mutation rights

| Value | May it be mutated? |
| --- | --- |
| Root passed to `track()`, `prepareReplace()`, `replicatedState()`, or `replace()` | No. Ownership moved to the tracker. |
| `change.state` and handles read from it | Yes, only while that change is open. After `prepare()`, `abort()`, or another adoption, every use throws. Writes through a handle whose element was removed from the draft are ignored. |
| External value after assigning or inserting it into a draft | Yes. The draft stored a validated clone. |
| `tracker.value`, `prepared.base`, retained older revisions | No. |
| `prepared.value`, `prepared.ops`, op tuples, paths, permutations, payloads | No. Payloads may be the same objects as parts of `prepared.value`. |
| `applyImmutable()` / `applyImmutableBatches()` inputs and result | No. The result shares containers with both inputs. |
| Values from replicated state and cells (`value`, listener values, in-process handles) | No. In-process consumers may share the provider's containers. |
| Mutable replica passed to `apply()` | Only through `apply()`, with batches it owns exclusively. Code that edits it between batches breaks convergence. |
| Batch passed to `apply()` | Consumed. `apply()` adopts payload containers into the replica. Use a detached copy for exactly one replica and never touch it again. |

## Replaying batches

Immutable replay is the preferred in-process path. One batch can fan out to any
number of immutable replicas:

```ts
let replica = tracker.value; // shared with authority; never mutated
// For each adopted batch, in order:
replica = applyImmutable(replica, prepared.ops); // replica must equal prepared.base
```

When only the final result of an ordered backlog is needed, replay its batches
without concatenating their operations. One copy-on-write scope is shared across
the complete call, so no intermediate revision is exposed or safe to retain:

```ts
replica = applyImmutableBatches(
  replica,
  queuedFrames.map((frame) => frame.ops),
);
```

Use separate `applyImmutable()` calls when every intermediate revision is
published or retained.

Mutable replay needs a detached starting root and a detached copy of every batch
for every replica. Never apply one in-memory batch to two mutable replicas:

```ts
import { apply } from "@earendil-works/chord/delta";

const detach = <T>(value: T): T => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as T;

let replica = detach(tracker.value); // exclusively owned starting root
// For each adopted batch, in order:
replica = apply(replica, detach(prepared.ops)); // fresh copy for this replica only
// Only apply() may change `replica`; do not edit it in application code.
```

Parsing a separately serialized message per replica is also a valid detachment.
`decode()` does not copy payloads, so decoding one in-memory `WireOp[]` for two
mutable replicas makes them alias each other.

## Do and don't

- Do build a fresh root and then transfer it; validate untrusted roots at your ingestion boundary.
- Do keep structural sharing between revisions, for example `replace(ctx, { ...state.value, changed })`.
- Do clone or serialize before handing any published value to code that may mutate it.
- Do settle every change with `prepare()` or `abort()`.
- Don't reuse one container at two places in a transferred root.
- Don't mutate anything the tracker owns, published, or received from a batch.
- Don't keep draft handles past their change or place a settled handle.
- Don't infer meaning from op shape. Only the resulting value is contractual.

## Roots and placements

Full roots are trusted. `track()` and `prepareReplace()` take ownership in O(1)
and never walk the tree. Roots must be alias-free, acyclic strict JSON: dense
plain arrays, plain or null-prototype objects with enumerable own data
properties, strings, booleans, finite numbers, and `null`. Violations have
unspecified behavior. For example, a container shared by two keys can make
`prepared.value` diverge from what replicas compute from `prepared.ops`.

Draft placements are copied, and that copy walk also validates. Placements come
from property writes, index writes, `push`, `unshift`, `splice`, `fill`, and
`copyWithin`. A non-strict value throws `TypeError` before the draft changes;
for example, `push(valid, invalid)` inserts nothing. Rejected values include:
cycles, accessors (never invoked), symbol keys, class instances, sparse or
non-plain arrays, functions, bigint, `NaN`, infinities, and `undefined`.
Null-prototype objects are accepted and preserved. Placing a draft handle clones
its current content. Placing one value at several paths yields independent
containers.

`undefined` rules:

- `draft.obj.key = undefined` deletes `key`.
- `arr[i] = undefined`, `push(undefined)`, `unshift`, `splice`, and `fill` with `undefined` throw.
- `undefined` nested anywhere inside a placed object or array throws. It is not dropped like `JSON.stringify` does.

Arrays stay dense. Writing past the next index and deleting an element throw.
Growing `length` inserts `null`; shrinking it removes elements.

## Lifecycle

`tracker.value` is the latest adopted revision. `beginChange()` opens an overlay
draft over it and never modifies it. A draft may stay open across `await`.
`prepare()` materializes the candidate and ops and does not change authority.
`adopt()` checks the preparation and swaps the root pointer.

Several changes may be open or prepared from one revision. Adopting one makes all
others stale: open drafts become unusable and their `prepare()` throws, and
prepared competitors are rejected by `adopt()`. `adopt()` also rejects foreign,
aborted, and already consumed preparations. `Change.abort()` or
`Prepared.abort()` after `prepare()` prevents adoption. The candidate stays
readable.

No-op batches:

- Empty `ops` means `prepared.value === prepared.base`. Writes restored to their original value and deeply equal container assignments usually normalize to empty.
- Equality ignores key order and prototype. A deeply equal assignment keeps the previous revision's order and prototype, even if the draft showed the new ones.
- Structural array edits may emit a nonempty exact batch even when the result is deeply equal.
- Adopting a no-op still advances `tracker.revision` and stales competitors. Replicated state does not publish no-ops.

`prepareReplace(value)` is a whole-root operation, not a diff. If `value` is
deeply equal to the current root, `ops` is empty and the current root is kept
(the comparison may traverse both trees). Otherwise `ops` is `[["r", value]]`
and `prepared.value === value`, so replicas receive the complete root.

Array mutators: `push`, `pop`, `shift`, `unshift`, `splice`, `reverse`, `sort`,
`fill`, and `copyWithin`. Held handles follow elements through reindexing.

## Operations

Paths contain object keys and non-negative integer array indices.

| Tuple | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["r", value]` | Replace the complete value. |
| `["s", path, value]` | Set an object property or array element. |
| `["d", path]` | Delete an object property or remove an array element. |
| `["a", path, text]` | Append to a string. |
| `["t", path, count]` | Remove `count` UTF-16 code units from a string's front. |
| `["p", path, index, remove, items]` | Splice an array. |
| `["m", path, permutation]` | Reorder an array: `new[i] = old[permutation[i]]`. |

Batches are exact but not canonical. The same change may use different tuples,
and large edit sets may fold into a region splice, an ancestor `s`, or `r`.

Reserved keys: the tracker never emits `__proto__`, `constructor`, or
`prototype` as a path segment. A mutation at or below such a key is folded into a
set of the nearest safe ancestor, or `r` at the root. `apply()`, `applyImmutable()`, `applyImmutableBatches()`, and `decoder()` reject
those segments with `UnsafePathError`.
The appliers write values as own data properties, never through a prototype setter.
Appliers check op shape and path safety but not payload strictness. Chord's
remote state applies batches decoded from JSON frames, so their payloads are strict
JSON; validate payloads of batches from any other source.

`encoder()` interns repeated paths into `WireOp` tuples; `decoder()` validates
and restores `Op` tuples. Use one encoder/decoder pair per ordered state stream.
Path IDs span batches and an `r` resets both dictionaries. After a decode or
apply error, discard the decoder and replica and recover from a later `r`.

## Limits and footguns

- No freezing. Mutating any immutable value corrupts state silently.
- In-process sharing: local handles, cell subscribers, and `replicatedState` subscribers receive the provider's containers. A consumer mutation corrupts authority and makes remote replicas diverge.
- A change inside a large flat array copies that array's pointer storage for the new revision.
- Placement validation costs time and memory on bulk inserts. In a benchmark unshifting 100k three-field objects, it added about 19 ms and 20 MiB of transient heap.
- Draft reads go through proxies. In one measurement, 20,000 hot nested reads took about 9 ms through the tracker versus 0.08 ms on raw objects; compare with `node --expose-gc packages/chord/test/delta-traversal.bench.ts --quick`.
- External proxies as placements, argument coercion callbacks that mutate the draft, non-primitive array indices, and non-numeric comparator results are out of contract. So are sort comparators that mutate, prepare, abort, or adopt. Behavior is unspecified.
- Object identity is not replicated. Each path is an independent value placement.
- One tracker is one revision sequence. Delivery order and persistence belong to the surrounding protocol.
"

"## [1.4.0] - 2026-10-21

### New Features

- **Image input for classifiers**: codemode `models.classify()` accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter. See [Use classifier models](docs/models.md#use-classifier-models) and [Codemode](docs/codemode.md#models).
- **Models Configuration reference**: every provider, model, model override, and compatibility field of `models.json`, generated from its schema. See [Models Configuration](docs/models-configuration.md).
- **Summaries without a fixed output cap**: compaction and branch summaries use the model's output limit, so long reasoning no longer makes them fail. See [Compaction](docs/compaction.md#compaction).
- **Codemode waits for a free worker**: parallel scripts and in-process subagents queue instead of failing, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` raises the limit. See [Codemode limits](docs/codemode.md#limits).
- **Rex terminal support**: OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and inline images.

### Added

- Added a Models Configuration reference generated from the `models.json` schema, listing all provider, model, model override, and compatibility fields ([#10790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10790))
- Codemode `models.classify()` now accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter, and lists Clef Omni and Jev 1.14 on Workers AI.
- Provider-level `compat` in `models.json` now also applies to classifier models, with the System One fields `imageInput` and `sendImageOptInHeader` for proxies that serve another service's classifiers. Extension classifier models accept `compat` too.
- Added `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` to the `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers, with thinking levels low through max ([#11121](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11121))
- Added support for the Rex terminal: OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and inline images ([#11131](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11131), [#11150](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11150) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), [#11183](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11183) by [@nihaals](https://github.com/nihaals))

### Changed

- Provider attribution headers now come from pi-ai's client identity. Extensions' `before_provider_headers` handlers no longer see the OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and OpenCode attribution headers; returning `null` for one still removes it. Cloudflare requests send pi's detailed `User-Agent` instead of `pi-coding-agent`, as do GitHub release checks for tool downloads, and OpenCode requests send `x-opencode-client` whenever attribution is enabled, not only with a session.
- `generateSummary()` and `generateSummaryWithUsage()` now ignore their `reserveTokens` parameter. Summary requests use the model's output limit instead.
- Changed the default GitHub Copilot model from `gpt-5.4`, which Copilot retired, to `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Changed the default NVIDIA model to `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b` ([#10910](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10910) by [@cv](https://github.com/cv))
- Changed the default Xiaomi model to `mimo-v2.6-pro` for the `xiaomi` and Xiaomi Token Plan providers, since `mimo-v2.5-pro` left the catalog.
- Grok 4.3 and Grok 4.5 on the `xai` provider now offer the `xhigh` thinking level.
- Sign in with ChatGPT: ChatGPT Business workspace usage-limit errors are not retried and tell the user to ask their workspace admin to increase the limit.

### Fixed

- Fixed compaction and branch summaries failing with "generation hit the token cap" when reasoning used most of the fixed summary output limit. Summaries now use the model's output limit, and `compaction.reserveTokens` only controls when compaction starts ([#9512](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9512), [#9075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9075)).
- Fixed `models.schema.json` missing descriptions for provider and model fields, so editors showed no hints for them ([#10790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10790))
- Fixed `pi update` failing with "Managed install marker is missing or invalid" when `managed-install.json` starts with a UTF-8 BOM, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds when it rewrites the file.
- Fixed HTML export showing literal asterisks for Markdown bold and italic next to CJK punctuation ([#3353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3353), [#10154](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10154))
- Fixed the terminal staying in mouse-tracking, focus-reporting, Kitty keyboard, and alternate-screen modes when pi exits without its normal terminal teardown, which flooded the shell prompt with escape sequences ([#11170](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11170))
- Fixed concurrent extension `select`/`confirm`/`input`/`editor` dialogs and inline `custom()` components in interactive mode: a second dialog replaced the first and the first promise never settled; closing the visible dialog now shows the previous one again ([#11166](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11166), [#9909](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9909))
- Fixed pasting in the shell hanging after copying text in pi and suspending it with Ctrl+Z on Linux: the background `wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel` process that keeps serving the clipboard was suspended along with pi ([#11179](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11179))
- Fixed codemode scripts failing immediately when both codemode workers are busy, for example with parallel codemode calls or in-process subagents. Scripts now wait up to 60 seconds for a free worker, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` raises the limit of two workers ([#11184](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11184))
- Fixed extensions failing to load when importing `@earendil-works/pi-ai/models` (e.g. for `clampThinkingLevel`) by exposing the subpath through the extension loader aliases and virtual modules ([#11156](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11156))
- Fixed `mcp.json` files that start with a UTF-8 BOM failing to parse, which skipped all their MCP servers and made `pi mcp add`/`pi mcp remove` fail ([#11191](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11191))
- Fixed `/compact <instructions>` ignoring the instructions when summarizing the start of a turn that compaction splits. When the split turn was the only new content since the last compaction, the instructions were ignored entirely ([#11058](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11058))
- Fixed resumed sessions and `/tree` navigation leaving extension tools inactive when the branch recorded its tools before they were registered, such as tools from extensions installed after the session started. Extension tools the branch never added or removed are now active unless they are registered with `defaultActive: false` ([#11062](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11062), [#11075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11075))
- Fixed sessions breaking after recovery from a response cut off at the output limit: the truncated tool call was omitted but its tool results were kept, so providers rejected every later request ([#11227](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11227), [#11233](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11233) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed the `grep` tool following `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, where options such as `--fixed-strings` silently changed regex searches into literal ones. The tool now runs `rg --no-config` ([#11203](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11203), [#11230](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11230) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed Windows shell detection rejecting runnable Microsoft Store shell aliases ([#9504](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9504) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed Windows shell detection missing PowerShell outside `PATH` and the legacy WSL `bash.exe` launcher when Windows is not installed in `C:\Windows`. pi now checks `%ProgramFiles%\PowerShell\7`, `%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0`, and `%SystemRoot%` ([#9501](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9501) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed GitHub Copilot sessions with large request bodies, such as many images, failing with HTTP 413 `failed to parse request` instead of compacting and retrying ([#11016](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11016) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed the `openai-codex` provider offering `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, which always fail for ChatGPT accounts ([#11173](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11173) by [@lucasmeijer](https://github.com/lucasmeijer))
- Fixed whitespace-only tool output (for example a bare `\r\n` from bash) making OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Google requests fail with a 400 ([#8720](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8720))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for more gateway upstream failures, `stream disconnected before completion` errors relayed by Codex CLI proxies, and transient Google Vertex OAuth token refresh failures, and retrying errors because of digits inside request ids or byte counts ([#10920](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10920), [#11057](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11057), [#10996](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10996))
- Fixed OpenAI Responses models losing the prompt cache on every deferred tool load after a tool was removed ([#10940](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10940))
- Fixed Cloudflare Workers AI classifier pricing: Clef Flash costs $0.038 and Jev $0.042 per million input tokens instead of Jev being listed as free.
- Fixed an unclosed `$$` display-math block swallowing or corrupting every Markdown table after it ([#11159](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11159))
- Fixed Markdown bold and italic not rendering next to CJK punctuation ([#10730](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10730) by [@theBucky](https://github.com/theBucky))
- Fixed `@` file autocomplete returning no results for queries containing regex metacharacters such as `[` or `(` ([#10972](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10972))"
